Question: Why do people look away from the camera in selfies? Is there any significance behind it?
Answer: It’s the same reason models might look away from the camera when being shot by a professional… the Look Away Pose is just a creative choice. This is also sometimes called the No Look Pose for those shots in which the subject makes no eye contact. People who shoot lots of selfies are sometimes bored with taking essentially the same shot many times a day. Some are influenced by fashion photography, model photography, portrait photography, or simply, the trends among other selfie-shooters. It might be used in fashion/ad photography to accentuate the product and not distract the view with the model’s terminal stare. Or it might be used by a photographer to coax a shy subject into maybe loosening up a bit before making eye contact. Of course, that’s the original purpose of the look, not necessarily applicable to selfies. They’re just using these styles. That’s it. No special significance. It might be intended suggest that the subject is interacting with something that’s out of the photo, or it might be used to convey various emotions. It might just be a trendy style apropos of nothing. Read More

Question: Why do they make chargers with USB C to USB C cable now instead of plain USB to USB-C like before?
Answer: It’s several basic things. First thing: Type-C is the current USB connector. Type-A (what you’re calling “plain” though no, it’s Type-A) is the legacy connector. Increasingly, devices will use Type-C and move away from Type-A. When you’re selling a new thing, you probably want it to support what’s happening today, sure, but also what’s happening over the lifetime of the device. Second thing: the Type-C connector, like the Micro-B connector, was engineered for the demands of the reality that we’re plugging things in and out all the time with USB, for charging. When USB was invented, it was designed to replace mouse, keyboard, printer, and modem connections on a desktop computer. So there wasn’t a huge thought given to longevity of connectors. The Type-A jack should last you 1,500 plug-unplug cycles if you don’t abuse it. The Type-C jack should last you 20,000 plugs/unplug cycles. Third thing: Type-C can support the new Power Delivery protocol. The power over USB was originally just to run small devices like keyboards and mice. That was up to 2.5W, which is actually way, way more than you’d need for a mouse or keyboard. When it became clear that USB was being used as a regular DC power supply for phones, they added the Battery Charging protocol. That could provide at least 7.5W over a special charging cable. The Power Delivery standard and Type-C with the high current cables can deliver +20V at 5A, or 100W, based on the original version of PD, and +48V at 5A, or 240W, with the latest improvements. Power supplies had to get smart for this, so your device has to “handshake” with the power brick and trade capacities, so you don’t accidently get 20V or 48V into a device that’s only good for 5V or 9V. That lets the blue smoke out… not good. Not every Type-C port is going to offer you 100W or 240W, but today’s “chargers” (they don’t actually do the charging, they just provide the power) can deliver the kind of power needed for tablets, laptops, monitors, etc. Not just phones, keyboards, and mice.

So he’s working on the “it wasn’t illegal when the President did it” argument. He’s got a friendly Supreme Court, so what could it hurt. The secondary effect of making this challenge in court was maybe even closer to the actual point of making the challenge: it shut down both Federal cases against Trump pending the ruling. So at this point, those cases may still make it to court in 2024, but they’re almost certain to not be concluded before Election Day in November. Maybe he can accept payment from other countries, or from large companies, for services rendered, as long as it’s an official act. Question: If Haley loses the Republican primary, can she be written in at the general election for president? Has any president been voted in by write-ins?
Answer: She can be written in for President, sure… if you’re in a state that allows this. The light green states… those allow write-ins the way most folks think write-ins work. You show up to the polling place and write the candidate’s name in. Those votes are tallied, and if that person has the most votes, they win the election. Those in green require a candidate to register as a write-in. If Nikki Haley wanted to be considered as a write-in candidate, she would have to register in each of these states. Otherwise, while you could certainly write-in her name, those votes wouldn’t be tallied. They go in the pile with voted for Mickey Mouse and Vermin Supreme. Finally, for the Presidential election, there probably is no write-in possible in the states shown as Orange, Red, or Brown. The Orange states allow registered write-ins for non-Presidential elections, but none for the Presidency. The Red states allow for write-ins only in the case of a substitute candidate who’s come along after the ballots were printed. In the brown states, “no” means “no” — no possible way to write in a candidate. So a Nikki Haley write-in campaign starts without access to 54 electoral votes. That’s of course on top of being in competition with Trump in every state. The most likely effect of a really well organized write in campaign, just like an Independent or third party campaign, is that she splits a bit of the vote with Trump, doesn’t win a single state, but maybe hands a few to Biden. That’s the spoiler effect in our winner-take-all system. It’s unlikely that she’d win any Democratic votes, and most anti-Trump Conservatives are going to vote against Trump rather than pick an alternate candidate, that vote increasing the likelihood that Trump wins. No President has won via write-ins. No President has even come close. No write-in for President has ever claimed a single electoral vote… but hey, there’s always a first time, and Trump is an unusually unpopular and hated candidate, as the primaries are demonstrating even as he wins with significant margins. If even 20% of Republicans nationwide who chose Trump in 2020 didn’t vote for Trump in the 2024, Biden would win every swing state and a whole new set of states would become “swingers,” including Florida and Texas. In fact, no President has won on with a Party other then the Republicans or Democrats since Zachery Taylor in 1848. His Vice President, Millard Filmore, was the last person to hold the Presidency not affiliated with the Republicans or the Democrats, after Taylor died of cholera in 1850. At the time, the Democrats and the Whigs were the two strong parties in the USA mandated by the mathematics of our voting system — the only point of stability is two strong parties. So even this was business as usual, though the Whig Party fell apart shortly after this last stand. It will not be any different in 2024.

Question: Are there any external USB drives that have both USB-C and Thunderbolt ports, or do you have to choose between them when purchasing one?
Answer: All Thunderbolt 3 and Thunderbolt 4 ports are Type-C ports. USB 3 can use Type-C, and USB 4 requires Type-C, but there is a distinction between “USB data protocols” and “Type-C connectors.” With USB4, all things are sadly optional. A USB4 port has to support USB 2.0 protocols. It can also support any or all USB 3 or Thunderbolt protocols, it can also support Power Deliver (eg, higher power specs) where applicable. But it doesn’t have to. All Thunderbolt 4 devices have to support the whole schmegegge: USB 2, 3, Thunderbolt, PD. So if you want a truly universal device, buy a Thunderbolt 4 device. I’m convinced that’s the only reason Intel kept Thunderbolt 4 as a separate thing: the USB folks made every piece of the spec optional. You could technically buy a USB4 drive, and I think it would have to have a Type-C connector, but it could only support USB 2 data protocols.
